title: Tensor closure for a fixed Galois partition
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a scheme [def-pc-scheme] admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), and let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian $\Lambda$-algebra. Work with sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant ring sheaf $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on the small etale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Fix a finite locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification] of $X$ by connected reduced subschemes $S_i$, and for each $i$ a connected finite etale surjection $V_i\to S_i$ with a finite group acting simply transitively on every geometric fibre; call this data $\mathcal P$. Let $\mathcal W_{\mathcal P}(A)$ consist of those module sheaves $E$ whose inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] to each $S_i$ is a filtered colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of sheaves admitting finite filtrations by subsheaves, with successive quotients locally constant $A_{S_i}$-module sheaves whose inverse images to $V_i$ are constant. Here locally constant means isomorphic to a constant module sheaf after an etale covering, and neither the constant values nor the sheaves in the filtrations are required to be finitely generated. For all $E,G\in\mathcal W_{\mathcal P}(A)$, the ordinary sheaf tensor product $E\otimes_{A_X}G$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] belongs to $\mathcal W_{\mathcal P}(A)$. No flatness assumption is imposed on either factor; this assertion concerns ordinary tensor product.

source.place: Expose XVII, 7.2.3-7.2.5 and Definitions 7.3.2-7.3.3, pp. 301-304; Proposition 11.3.4 and Proposition 11.2.1(i),(vii),(x),(xi), pp. 328-330. Tensor-filtration consequence of the discrete local-system/ind-unipotent description, used in Lemma 7.6.11.

proof.text: Fix a nonempty stratum $j:S\to X$ and write $c:V\to S$ for its chosen cover. Constant-coefficient restriction is the exact module inverse image of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. Its ring comparison identifies $j^{-1}A_X$ with $A_S$, so [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] gives $j^*(E\otimes_{A_X}G)\cong j^*E\otimes_{A_S}j^*G$. The hypotheses on $\mathcal W_{\mathcal P}(A)$ already give filtered-colimit presentations of these two restrictions by finite-filtered sheaves. It is therefore enough to prove the corresponding assertion on $S$ with its one fixed cover; no refinement of the partition will be made.

Choose a geometric point $\bar v$ of $V$, with image $\bar s$, and put $\Pi=\pi_1(S,\bar s)$ and $H=c_*\pi_1(V,\bar v)$. By [lem-per-torsion-local-system-monodromy], every generator whose pullback to $V$ is constant is a local system; its monodromy has trivial $H$-action. The same node says that ambient extensions of torsion local systems and all their small colimits remain local systems, and that stalks give an exact equivalence preserving colimits. It applies here because $\ell A=0$ and $S$ is connected Noetherian. Thus every finite-filtered term in the two presentations is a local system whose discrete monodromy module has a finite $\Pi$-stable filtration with $H$ acting trivially on its quotients. Conversely every such filtration corresponds to a finite filtration by subsheaves with quotients constant on $V$: exactness transports the submodules and quotients, the pullback clause makes their pullbacks constant, and $V\to S$ is itself an etale covering witnessing local constancy.

For two finite-filtered terms $L,M$ write their monodromy modules as $U,W$, with filtrations $0=U_0\subset\cdots\subset U_r=U$ and $0=W_0\subset\cdots\subset W_s=W$. Their tensor is a local system with monodromy $U\otimes_A W$ and diagonal action by [lem-per-local-system-tensor-monodromy]. For integers $k$ define $T_k$ to be the sum of the images of $U_a\otimes_A W_b$ for $a+b\le k$, $0\le a\le r$, $0\le b\le s$. These are $\Pi$-stable submodules, $T_0=0$ and $T_{r+s}=U\otimes_AW$; if one filtration has length zero its module and the tensor are zero. For $h\in H$, $u\in U_a,w\in W_b$,
$$(h-1)(u\otimes w)=(hu-u)\otimes hw+u\otimes(hw-w)\in T_{a+b-1}.$$
Here $hu-u\in U_{a-1}$, $hw-w\in W_{b-1}$, and $hw\in W_b$; terms with $a=0$ or $b=0$ vanish. Since pure tensors generate the images, $H$ acts trivially on every $T_k/T_{k-1}$. This uses only the tensor relations and generators of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; it never identifies a graded quotient with a tensor of graded quotients.

source.place: Tensor-filtration consequence of 7.3.2 and 11.1.1; explicit elementary convolution calculation.

proof.text: Apply the exact monodromy equivalence and its pullback criterion [lem-per-torsion-local-system-monodromy] to the filtration $T_k$ from Step 3. It becomes a finite filtration by subsheaves of $L\otimes_{A_S}M$. Every quotient pulls back to a constant sheaf on $V$, and is therefore locally constant on $S$ by that etale covering. Hence the tensor of any two finite-filtered terms is again one of the finite-filtered objects allowed in the definition of $\mathcal W$. No subobject closure of arbitrary etale sheaves is being used: these are submodules within the exact local-system equivalence.

Write $j^*E=\varinjlim_{\alpha\in I}L_\alpha$ and $j^*G=\varinjlim_{\beta\in J}M_\beta$ with small filtered index categories. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] with coefficient category $\operatorname{Mod}_A$, its usual additive closed symmetric tensor, and an essentially small model of $S_{\mathrm{et}}$. Its sheaf tensor is the ordinary constant-ring tensor here: [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor], applied to constant presheaves and then to the module presheaves, identifies both with sheafification of the sectionwise balanced tensor. Thus its colimit-preservation assertion gives
$$j^*E\otimes_{A_S}j^*G\cong\varinjlim_{(\alpha,\beta)\in I\times J}(L_\alpha\otimes_{A_S}M_\beta).$$
The product category is small and filtered: nonemptiness, cocones for two objects and equalization of parallel arrows are supplied coordinatewise by $I$ and $J$. Step 4 makes every term finite-filtered with the required constant-on-$V$ quotients. This is exactly the required filtered-colimit presentation.

Repeat Steps 1-5 for each stratum. The restriction of $E\otimes_{A_X}G$ then has the required presentation on every $S_i$, which is the definition of membership in $\mathcal W_{\mathcal P}(A)$. For empty $X$ there are no strata and this condition is vacuous. The construction keeps the original covers and allows arbitrary constant module values, zero modules and zero filtration lengths. At no point is injectivity of $U_a\otimes W_b\to U\otimes W$ needed: its image defines $T_k$. Therefore no flatness condition has entered.
